- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 88–90 range) and then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the 30-day window — forecasts often fail to capture the tendency to return to prior 10–15 day averages.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — underestimates downward moves until 2–3 days after they occur.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, especially when recent prices are high.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven volatility — e.g., EU ETS auction cycles or regulatory changes — leading to persistent bias in mid-to-late forecast.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
- When true outcome is below 80, model often overcorrects upward, suggesting a ceiling bias in downward moves.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — fails to weight recent 5–7 day data adequately, leading to lagged reactions to new information.
